title: Clash agent product benchmark v1 — runnable surfaces and explicit contract gaps

cases.title: Import an exact Project image Asset

outcome.objective: Import inputs/exact-source.svg through Clash as the immutable Project image Asset `benchmark-asset-exact-import-v1`; preassign that exact identity in the import call. Preserve the fixture byte-for-byte, list the Project Assets, read that same Asset back, and submit the original SVG as the exact media evidence plus a short review containing the returned Project Asset identity.
acceptanceCriteria: The SVG is imported through the real Clash Asset surface rather than represented by a handwritten record.
The imported Project Asset is active, resolves as image media, and its Host-delivered bytes exactly match inputs/exact-source.svg.
A successful import, list, and get are present in the Agent trajectory.
The immutable fixture remains a normal workspace file and the submission paths stay inside the isolated workspace.

deliverables.description: The exact SVG file imported as the Project Asset
Project Asset identity and semantic readback notes; the runner owns exact-byte verification

checks.detail: The packaged Clash CLI and MCP Asset dispatcher import a workspace file into the selected Project.
The benchmark runner independently lists and reads Project Assets, retains the opaque Host receipt, and hashes Host-delivered bytes.

productReadback.description: Match one active Project image Asset to the submitted SVG by exact SHA-256 and retain its opaque Host receipt.

cases.title: Trash and restore a Project Asset safely

outcome.objective: Import inputs/exact-source.svg as Project image Asset `benchmark-asset-trash-restore-v1`; preassign that exact identity in the import call, read it before mutation, trash it, read the trashed state, restore it through Clash, and read the final active state. Submit the unchanged SVG as media evidence and a lifecycle review containing the stable Project Asset identity.
acceptanceCriteria: The same Project Asset identity is used for import, trash, restore, and final readback.
Both guarded lifecycle mutations occur through Clash after the required reads; no force or fabricated receipt is used.
Trusted Host readback finds one final active image Asset whose bytes exactly match the fixture.
The trajectory contains successful import, list, get, trash, and restore product operations.

deliverables.description: The exact SVG bytes of the final restored Project Asset
Stable identity and observed active-to-trashed-to-active lifecycle

checks.detail: The packaged Asset CLI and MCP dispatcher expose read-before-write trash and restore with no force bypass.
The runner independently confirms final active state, media kind, exact delivered bytes, and the opaque Host receipt.

productReadback.description: Match the final active Project image Asset to the submitted SVG by exact SHA-256 after the traced trash and restore operations.

outcome.objective: Create a compact editable Director Stage with an establishing beat, a motivated action beat, and a close reaction beat. Use at least three objects, three cameras, three ordered shots, and one changing animation track, then capture one real Director PNG at each beat and preserve the Stage plus a short review.
acceptanceCriteria: The Stage is schema-valid and every object, camera, shot, active-camera, and animation reference resolves.
Three ordered shots visibly cover establishing, action, and reaction beats with distinct cameras.
Exactly three submitted evidence images are real Director capture outputs associated with the persisted Stage revision.
The Stage mutation, readback, and captures are present in the Agent trajectory.

checks.detail: The Project Host returns the persisted Director Stage and signed revision receipt.
The Director product renderer produces exact-time PNGs with Stage revision verification.

productReadback.description: Read back the persisted Stage and three Director capture receipts from distinct creative beats.

cases.title: Medium Director, Remotion, and Timeline functional regression

outcome.objective: Create a 9-second 1080x1080 functional integration composition that combines one editable Director Stage, exact-time Director captures, one original editable Remotion TSX character persisted through Canvas, and one canonical Timeline that uses both product sources. Persist every source through Clash, render the final Timeline, sample three frames, and document the Stage-to-Canvas-to-Timeline lineage. This case evaluates functional correctness and lineage only; it does not require a content-quality review.
acceptanceCriteria: The persisted Director Stage contains at least four objects, two cameras, three ordered sequence shots, and one animated track whose values change.
The exact self-contained Remotion TSX is persisted as a Canvas remotion-component, and its stable node ID is reused unchanged as the sourceNodeId of a custom remotion Timeline composition item.
After persisting the Remotion component, read it through the public `canvas.get` operation and use that read-back stable node ID unchanged as the Timeline composition item's sourceNodeId.

The canonical Timeline contains at least three tracks and five items across at least 270 frames, including image, composition, and text item types; every media item preserves the actual kind of its referenced Project Asset.

After creating the Timeline, read it through the public `timeline.get` operation, make a real subsequent edit by adding the closing title, and persist that new revision through `timeline.save`; the save must not be a no-op.

For exact lineage, a Director capture receipt binds its projectAssetId output to the final Stage revision, and a canonical Timeline media item references that same projectAssetId; the Stage is not mutated to store its own Action output.
The product renderer completes a decodable 1080x1080 video of approximately 9 seconds, and three frames are sampled from that final video.
The completed render Project Asset is retrieved through the public Asset read surface to produce the final-video deliverable; internal Host HTTP endpoints are not part of the agent workflow.
Trusted readback matches the final Stage revision and capture receipt, exact Canvas component source, Timeline revision and sourceNodeId, and completed final render Asset.

deliverables.description: Exact-time PNG captured from the Director Stage
Opening frame sampled from the final video
Action frame sampled from the final video
Closing frame sampled from the final video

outcome.objective: Discover one native GeneratorDefinition that registers multiple Actions, create a Project Generator revision, invoke two distinct Actions from that same frozen revision, and preserve each ActionRun and exact single OutputCommit.
acceptanceCriteria: The Agent selects Actions through a native Generator CLI or MCP contract rather than a legacy Canvas badge.
Both Runs pin the same Generator revision while retaining distinct actionId, actionRunId, and invocation fingerprint identities.
Each successful Run has exactly one independently readable OutputCommit.
Trusted readback verifies the Definition, Generator revision, Runs, and outputs.

checks.detail: No native Generator CLI or MCP dispatcher is exposed to the Agent yet.
The benchmark runner has no trusted Generator revision, ActionRun, and OutputCommit readback yet.

productReadback.description: Future trusted readback for one frozen Generator revision, two ActionRuns, and their exact OutputCommits.

outcome.objective: Create a mutable Project Generator head, materialize one output, attempt an incompatible in-place revision, fork it through copy-on-write, and replay the original invocation without duplicating its public ActionRun or OutputCommit.
acceptanceCriteria: The materialized Generator rejects the incompatible in-place change and preserves its original revision.
The fork remains in the same Definition family and records forkedFrom without rewriting old downstream references.
Exact replay returns the original terminal ActionRun and OutputCommit instead of creating a private task again.
Trusted readback proves both Generator heads and the stable replay lineage.

checks.detail: No Generator CLI or MCP contract exposes head advance, COW fork, and exact replay to an Agent.
No trusted benchmark readback can yet verify Generator heads, forkedFrom, replayed Run identity, and OutputCommit uniqueness.

productReadback.description: Future trusted readback for source and forked Generator heads plus one idempotently replayed Run and OutputCommit.

outcome.objective: Create a standard mutable Document Asset, advance its head through CAS while preserving the first immutable revision, attach the Document to a Project Asset, and advance the attachment to the new exact revision.
acceptanceCriteria: Both immutable Document revisions remain independently readable with one stable Document identity.
The head advances only through the expected revision CAS and no force bypass exists.
The attachment pins an exact Document revision before being explicitly advanced.
Trusted readback verifies the revision chain, body references, and attachment history.

deliverables.description: Exact attachment and revision history review

checks.detail: No Document Asset CLI or MCP dispatcher exposes create, CAS advance, history, and attachment operations.
The benchmark runner has no trusted Document revision, body, and attachment readback.

productReadback.description: Future trusted readback for immutable Document revisions, head CAS, and exact attachment history.

cases.title: ASR Generator to transcript Document contract

outcome.objective: Import one audio source, invoke the native clash.asr Generator transcribe Action, wait for its public ActionRun to finish, and preserve the exact timed-transcript Document output with producer and source references.
acceptanceCriteria: The ASR operation is invoked through the native Generator Agent surface with one frozen audio Asset reference.
The public Run progresses asynchronously and publishes exactly one media.transcript Document OutputCommit.
The Document contains timed words and pins the ActionRun producer plus exact source Asset revision.
Trusted readback verifies the Run, OutputCommit, Document body, and lineage.

checks.detail: clash.asr is registered internally, but no native Generator CLI or MCP dispatcher lets an Agent create and follow its Run.
The benchmark runner cannot yet independently read back the ASR ActionRun, OutputCommit, and timed-transcript Document lineage.

productReadback.description: Future trusted readback for native ASR Run, exact OutputCommit, timed transcript body, producer, and source references.
